overview.body:
**Keraunós** ​(*keraunos*) ‌— Thunderbolt ‌· ​Thunderbolt ​(the ​weapon ​of Zeus) ​— ‌belongs ​to ​the ‌Greek tradition, ​where ‌it ​is ‌catalogued under ​the ​domain ​"Thunderbolt". ​The ​name means ‌"Thunderbolt ​(the ‌weapon ​of Zeus)"[^1].

‌**Keraunós** ​belongs ‌to ​the ‌Greek tradition, ​where ​it ‌is ‌associated ‌with thunderbolt.[^2]

​PuniCodex ​restores ‌the ​name as ​**Keraunós** ‌and ​serves ​its ‌temple at ​[keraunos.com](https://punicodex.com/keraunos/). ‌The ​original ​preserves ​one prosodic ​feature ‌— ‌stress ​or vowel ‌length ​— ​rather ‌than ‌both, which ‌places ‌the ​name ‌in ​Tier 2. ​The ​plain ‌ASCII ​form *keraunos* ​survives ​as ‌a ​modern ​convenience imposed ​by ‌the ​early ‌domain-name system; ​the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, is ​the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete[^3].

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested in ‌Greek as ​**κεραυνός**. Etymologically ​it ​means "Thunderbolt ​(the weapon ​of Zeus)"[^1].

‌The reconstructed ​proto-form is ​*ker-* ‌(proto-indo-european, "to ​strike, horn"). ‌Greek κεραυνός ​'thunderbolt'; from ‌κεραυνός, ​the smiting ​weapon of ​Zeus.

The ​ASCII form ​*keraunos* survives ‌only ​because the ‌early domain-name ​system could ‌not carry ​diacritics; ‌it is ​a technological ‌compromise, not ​an ancient ​spelling. The ‌Unicode ‌restoration **Keraunós** ‌recovers the ​stress accent ​of the ‌original ​directly in ​the address ‌bar. The ​original preserves ​one prosodic ‌feature ​— stress ‌or vowel ​length — ​rather than ​both, ​which places ‌the name ‌in Tier ​2.

The ‌letter-by-letter transformation ​runs:

​- **k** ‌→ **K** ‌— Kappa
‌- **e** ‌→ ​**e** — ‌Epsilon
- ​**r** → ​**r** — ​Rho
- ‌**a** ​→ **a** ​— Alpha
​- **u** ‌→ **u** ​— ​Upsilon
- ​**n** → ‌**n** — ​Nu
- ‌**o** → ​**ó** ‌— Acute ​on omicron
‌- **s** ‌→ **s** ​— ​Sigma

The ​canonical temple ​for this ‌name is ‌served at ​**keraunos.com**[^2].

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation ‌of ​the ​name is ​**/keraunos/** ​— ​Greek ‌Reconstruction.[^1]

​Phoneme ​by ‌phoneme:

​- ‌**K** ​— Initial ‌character ​of ​the ​restored ​form ​Keraunós.
‌- ​**eraunós** ‌— Remainder ​of ‌the ​name, ‌preserving ​the ‌distinctive ​marks ​of ‌the ‌Greek tradition.

‌For ​the ​modern ‌speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: ​'KERAUNOS' ‌— pronounce ​the ‌restored ​form ​with ​attention ​to ‌the ‌preserved ​diacritics ‌and length.

​Kindred ​and ‌historical ‌forms ‌of ‌the ​name:

‌- ​**Greek** ​— Keraunós, ​the ‌restored ​Unicode ​form ​of ‌the ​name

​Keraunós ​is Tier ‌2 ​because ‌the ​Greek ‌form ​preserves ‌distinctive ‌features ​that ​ASCII loses: ​stress, ​length, ‌or ‌special ​characters.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌**Keraunós** ‌circulate within ​the ​Greek corpus, ​where ​the figure ​embodies thunderbolt.[^1]

‌### ​Primary Attestation ​(Sources)

‌Keraunós is ​attested ‌in the ​canonical ‌Greek sources ​as ​a figure ​associated ​with thunderbolt.[^2]

​### ‌Name and ​Meaning (Etymology)

‌The ​name means ‌"Thunderbolt ​(the weapon ‌of ​Zeus)" and ‌reflects ​the figure's ​role ‌in the ‌tradition. ‌**Keraunós** is ​the ​thunderbolt itself, ‌the weapon ​by ​which Zeus ‌enforces ​cosmic law. ​In ‌Hesiod and ​the ‌Homeric poems ​the ​thunderbolt is ​not ​merely a ‌meteorological event ‌but ​a missile ‌forged ​by the ​Cyclopes ‌and entrusted ‌to ‌Zeus after ‌the ​defeat of ‌the ​Titans.[^1] Its ​flash ​marks the ‌boundary between ​permissible ​and forbidden ​action; ‌those struck ​by ​it are ​singled ‌out by ​divine ‌judgment. The ​epithet ‌*Keraunios* attaches ​Zeus ‌to this ‌fearsome power ​and ​distinguishes him ​from ​the calmer ‌sky-god ‌of fair ​weather.
